payload.title: Punta Cana Destination Wedding Guide
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, who have seen Punta Cana resort weddings online and want to know, before they commit to a long-haul Caribbean wedding, whether they can marry legally in the Dominican Republic or should marry at home first and hold a symbolic ceremony on the beach, when the weather and hurricane season make sense, what their guests flying from Australia need to know about entry and safety, and what to ask a resort so their day is private and well run rather than one of several on the same sand.
payload.goal: Book a Wedded Concierge consultation (speak with a Wedded Advisor) at /wonderland-concierge.
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'punta cana destination wedding' are led by resort, package and local planner pages written for North American couples, with the legal side thin, undated or copied between sites, the weather described as 'perfect all year', and hurricane season and long-haul guest travel from Australia barely mentioned. This guide is written for Australians and is honest about the choice they actually face: marry legally in the Dominican Republic only as official Dominican sources (Junta Central Electoral and civil registry, foreign ministry or consulate) and Smartraveller state, or marry legally at home and hold a symbolic ceremony in Punta Cana, with Australian recognition taken from the AGD and Smartraveller facts we already hold; when to go from official climate normals (ONAMET or WMO WWIS, station and period named) and the US National Hurricane Center's Atlantic season dates; guests from Australia from Smartraveller entry and safety advice, dated; and, because Punta Cana weddings are resort-led, the venue questions page-one results skip: other weddings that day, beach ceremony rules, heat and shade, older guests' access, the wet weather plan, and registry timing as the couple's own responsibility. No resort names, no rankings, no prices. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
outline_spine: Intro: direct answer in the first 100 words (Australian couples can plan a Punta Cana wedding either by marrying legally in the Dominican Republic as official sources set out, or by marrying legally at home and holding a symbolic ceremony there; season and guest travel shape the date), then exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways.
Why Punta Cana: the setting on the Dominican Republic's east coast and why weddings there are resort-led; no venue or resort names, no rankings, no 'best'.

Marrying legally in the Dominican Republic or a symbolic ceremony: civil marriage requirements only as the Junta Central Electoral / civil registry, the Dominican foreign ministry or a Dominican consulate, and Smartraveller (getting married overseas; Dominican Republic) state; any step not officially sourced becomes 'check with the Dominican authorities' and a booking-checklist item; Australian recognition of overseas marriages from the AGD and Smartraveller facts already held; 'general information as at November 2026, not legal advice' once; link /expert-advice/should-you-marry-legally-abroad-or-have-a-symbolic-ceremony and /destination-weddings/weddings-abroad-where-can-you-legally-get-married.

When to go: official climate normals (ONAMET or WMO World Weather Information Service) for Punta Cana or the nearest station, station and period named; Atlantic hurricane season dates from the US National Hurricane Center; no 'best month'.

Guests travelling from Australia: Smartraveller Dominican Republic entry requirements and safety advice, dated; no flight times, routes or airlines; link /destination-weddings/destination-wedding-timeline for when to tell guests.

Planning your Punta Cana wedding: the venue questions (other weddings on the same day, beach ceremony rules and permissions, heat and shade at ceremony time, access for older guests, the wet weather plan, and registry or paperwork timing as the couple's responsibility); link /destination-weddings/how-to-plan-a-destination-wedding and /destination-weddings/all-inclusive-wedding-cost (no figures).
Close: one Wedded Advisor line from brand-facts 'Claims we can make' (closing CTA to /wonderland-concierge); nothing implying the Advisor handles legal paperwork.
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words, then exactly 4 Key takeaways, each one concise sentence, no figures, no prices.
Why Punta Cana: setting and the resort-led nature of weddings there, with no venue or resort names and no rankings.

Marrying legally in the Dominican Republic vs a symbolic ceremony, stated only from official sources (Junta Central Electoral / civil registry, Dominican foreign ministry or consulate, Smartraveller); unsourced steps written as 'check with the Dominican authorities' and added to the booking checklist; 'general information as at November 2026, not legal advice' once.

Australian recognition of overseas marriages only from the AGD and Smartraveller facts already held (reuse from the symbolic-ceremony source pack); never state that the Dominican Republic requires a CNI, apostille or translation unless an official source says so.
When to go: official climate normals with station and period named (ONAMET or WMO WWIS), and Atlantic hurricane season dates from the US National Hurricane Center.
Guests from Australia: Smartraveller Dominican Republic entry and safety advice, dated; no flight times or routes.
Planning as venue questions: other weddings that day, beach ceremony rules, heat and shade, older guests' access, wet weather plan, registry timing as the couple's responsibility.

Internal links once each: /destination-weddings/weddings-abroad-where-can-you-legally-get-married, /expert-advice/should-you-marry-legally-abroad-or-have-a-symbolic-ceremony, /destination-weddings/how-to-plan-a-destination-wedding, /destination-weddings/destination-wedding-timeline, /destination-weddings/all-inclusive-wedding-cost (no figures). FAQ section. Close with one Wedded Advisor line from brand-facts 'Claims we can make' linking /wonderland-concierge.
avoid: Any price, fee amount, DOP, USD or AUD figure, 'from' price, percentage, statistic or processing time, including FAQ, meta and takeaways.
'Best' anywhere (best resort, best month, best beach) and any ranking.
Resort, venue, vendor, planner, officiant, lawyer or airline names and any business contact details.
Flight times, routes, stopovers or airlines.
Legal steps, document lists, waiting periods, residency rules or beach ceremony rules not traced to an official Dominican or Australian government page.
Any statement of the legal position for same-sex couples.
Any Advisor or Wedded Wonderland role in legal paperwork, registry filing, translations or apostilles; Wedded Privileges, room blocks, 'free', availability promises.
'Perfect weather all year' or any weather claim without an official station source; hurricane dates from any source other than the National Hurricane Center.
Research talk in copy (what we could or could not find, sources or method); hedge stacking.
Competitor wedding sites, resort or package sellers, directories, forums or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording, claims or images (including Easy Weddings).
US spelling, em dashes, exclamation marks, cliches, 'last dance'.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.

payload.intro_plan: Open on the reader's position (Punta Cana is on the list, it is a long way from Australia, and they want to know it will be legal, well timed and private), answer directly in the first 100 words, then the 4 takeaways.
payload.key_takeaways_rule: Exactly 4 bullets, each a single concise sentence, no figures, no prices, no research talk.
key_takeaways_plan: You can marry legally in the Dominican Republic by following the official civil process, or marry legally at home first and hold a symbolic ceremony in Punta Cana.
Check the Atlantic hurricane season and the official climate averages before you choose your date.
Point your guests to Smartraveller for Dominican Republic entry and safety advice well before they book.
Ask your resort about other weddings that day, beach ceremony rules, shade, access and the wet weather plan before you commit.
